content: 1. Elevated gastric pH caused by omeprazole may lead to premature dissolution of budesonide products, potentially altering their release characteristics and absorption in the duodenum. 2. Butabarbital reduces the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of omeprazole by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 3. Butalbital similarly decreases omeprazole levels or effects via CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 4. Omeprazole increases cannabidiol levels or effects by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 5. Cannabidiol increases omeprazole levels or effects by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Dose reduction of sensitive CYP2C19 substrates should be considered when co-administered with cannabidiol. 6. Omeprazole reduces the effects of capecitabine through an unknown mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Retrospective data suggest that elevated gastric pH from PPI use may impair capecitabine tablet dissolution and absorption. 7. Carbamazepine decreases omeprazole levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 8. Omeprazole reduces the levels or effects of carbonyl iron by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 9. Omeprazole decreases the effects of cefpodoxime by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 10. Omeprazole decreases the effects of cefuroxime by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 11. Cenobamate decreases omeprazole levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Cenobamate also increases omeprazole levels or effects by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Dose reduction of CYP2C19 substrates should be considered when co-administered with cenobamate. 12. Omeprazole reduces ciprofloxacin levels or effects through an unknown mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Co-administration with omeprazole slightly diminishes ciprofloxacin ER tablet absorption (by 20%). 13. Omeprazole increases citalopram levels or effects by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. The maximum recommended dose of citalopram for patients taking CYP2C19 inhibitors is 20 mg/day due to the risk of QT prolongation. 14. Omeprazole increases clobazam levels or effects by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Dosage adjustment may be required as CYP2C19 inhibitors can increase exposure to N-desmethylclobazam, the active metabolite. 15. Cobicistat increases omeprazole levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 16. Conivaptan increases omeprazole levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 17. Omeprazole reduces crizotinib levels or effects by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Drugs that elevate gastric pH may decrease crizotinib solubility and bioavailability, though no formal studies have been conducted. 18. Long-term use of PPIs, including omeprazole, may cause hypomagnesemia, increasing the risk of toxicity when co-administered with cyclosporine. Caution and monitoring are advised. 19. Omeprazole reduces dabrafenib levels or effects by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Drugs that alter upper GI tract pH, such as PPIs, H2-blockers, and antacids, may decrease dabrafenib solubility and bioavailability. 20. Dabrafenib decreases omeprazole levels or effects by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Alternative treatments should be considered if available. 21. Omeprazole reduces the time to Tmax for amphetamine and dextroamphetamine due to reduced gastric acidity caused by PPIs. However, the AUC remains unaffected. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 22. Omeprazole increases diazepam buccal levels or effects by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Strong or moderate CYP2C19 inhibitors may decrease the rate of diazepam elimination, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 23. Omeprazole increases diazepam intranasal levels or effects by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Strong or moderate CYP2C19 inhibitors may decrease the rate of diazepam elimination, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 24. Both dichlorphenamide and omeprazole decrease serum potassium levels. Caution and monitoring are advised. 25. Omeprazole increases digoxin toxicity risk due to prolonged PPI use causing hypomagnesemia. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 26. Efavirenz increases omeprazole levels or effects by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism and decreases omeprazole levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 27. Elagolix increases omeprazole levels or effects by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Elagolix is a weak CYP2C19 inhibitor, and no dose adjustments are needed for omeprazole doses of 40 mg/day or less. Elagolix also decreases omeprazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 28. Omeprazole increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Due to incomplete information on eluxadoline metabolism, caution is recommended when co-administered with strong CYP2C19 inhibitors. 29. Encorafenib affects omeprazole metabolism by both inhibiting and inducing CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may increase toxicity or reduce efficacy. 30. Omeprazole increases escitalopram levels or effects by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 31. Eslcarbazepine acetate increases omeprazole levels or effects by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 32. Etravirine increases omeprazole levels or effects by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 33. Fedratinib increases omeprazole levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Adjust doses of CYP3A4 substrates as necessary. 34. Omeprazole reduces ferric gluconate levels or effects by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 35. Omeprazole reduces ferric maltol levels or effects by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 36. Omeprazole reduces ferrous fumarate levels or effects by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 37. Omeprazole reduces ferrous gluconate levels or effects by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 38. Omeprazole reduces ferrous sulfate levels or effects by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 39. Fexinidazole increases omeprazole levels or effects by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 40. Omeprazole increases finerenone levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Monitor serum potassium during initiation and dosage adjustment of either finerenone or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Adjust finerenone dosage as needed. 41. Omeprazole increases flibanserin levels or effects by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required.
